make each run better than the last. The founders getting real leverage
aren't aiming agents at busywork, they're rebuilding core workflows,
so choose your scaffolding as carefully as your model. 

 AI JUST TOOK 40 OF THE APP STORE'S TOP 100 (4 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 AI has crossed from hype into real consumer spending. More than 40 of
the top 100 App Store apps now have AI features built in, and they
grew sales four times faster than the rest of the top 100, inside a
$1.4 trillion market. What's pulling the money is that an AI upgrade
pays off the instant you buy it, a higher limit or a smarter coach, so
the spending is landing on everyday apps like photos, health, and
shopping, not just the chatbots. 

🧠 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 YOUR AI STRATEGY HAS A TRUST PROBLEM, NOT A TOOLING PROBLEM (11
MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Many companies now have the technology they need to go faster. The
blocker is the systems companies design to prevent things from
happening. Rapid innovation can't happen in environments where
employees aren't trusted. Companies need employees with agency - the
ability to make decisions on behalf of the organization - or their AI
innovation efforts will be wasted. 

 THE INEVITABLE FAILURE OF ONE-SHOT PROJECT FUNDING (6 MINUTE READ)
[8] 

 Software requires ongoing investment, but this is a feature, not a
bug or mistake. Software is a depreciating intellectual asset, and
companies need to recognize and budget for this. Every line of code in
software needs to be supported until the last customer deletes it.
One-time project-based budgets ignore this reality, which inevitably
leads to financial and technical crises. 

 YOUR NEXT SEO HIRE IS A PRODUCT MANAGER (7 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Search is moving from ten blue links to AI answers, and the usual SEO
hire, a channel manager who files tickets and reports rankings, is
built for the old game. What works now is product thinking,
understanding what a person actually means when they ask, then shaping
the product so an AI model trusts it enough to cite. AI made the
technical grunt work cheap, so hire for judgment, the person who can
walk into a product review and defend a roadmap, not a keyword report.


⚒️ 

TOOLS & RESOURCES

 WORDPRESS.COM CHANGELOG: WORDPRESS 7.0 AND WAYS TO REPURPOSE YOUR
WRITTEN CONTENT (5 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 WordPress 7.0 shipped last month. WordPress.com sites have been
automatically updated. Changes include post previews, navigation
overlays, responsive block visibility, more design pieces, a font
manager, and much more. The release also ships with AI features
designed to assist in the editor, as well as real-time collaboration
on selected plans. 

 GOOGLE MEET'S AI NOTE-TAKER NOW LETS YOU CUSTOMIZE YOUR MEETING NOTES
AND TRACK DECISIONS (3 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Google has rolled out an upgrade to its 'Take notes for me' feature
in Google Meet that gives users more control over what gets captured,
making it easier to track outcomes after meetings wrap up. Users can
now toggle specific sections, like Decisions or Next Steps. The new
Decisions tracker helps to categorize outcomes like 'Aligned' or
'Needs Further Discussion'. The Summary section has been tightened up
to be more concise and scannable. Screenshots of the changes are
available in the article. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 WE ACCIDENTALLY BUILT A SECOND CODEBASE (10 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Skills are small bundles of instructions handed to models so they can
run the same workflows every time. Teams will often notice they keep
doing the same things every time, so they write the workflow down as a
skill and stop doing it by hand. Over time, this can result in a huge
library of skills. These skills will eventually become obsolete as
models improve. Developers need to monitor skill development so they
don't build up and become a second code base that nobody uses. 

 OUR FIRST CUSTOMERS WERE THE EXCEPTION (11 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 The market always wins, even if a great team has a great product. You
can't change a market, but you can always pivot to a more favorable
sector. This requires a high level of execution and can mean
essentially starting the company all over again.

 YC CEO Garry Tan recalls running low on Tesla charge in rural Texas

# PewDiePie Releases an Open-Source AI Platform

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5ce7dec9-1c69-4e88-a8e9-3b652d379fca/0608_Article_Photo_1.png?t=1780933066)
Caption: PewDiePie releases his free AI workspace / [PewDiePie](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAzT5lcezPs)

After a year of development, Felix “PewDiePie” Kjellberg recently launched Odysseus, a self-hosted AI workspace similar to Claude and ChatGPT’s UI—available [for free](https://pewdiepie-archdaemon.github.io/odysseus/).

**Why it matters:** Major creators are finding ways to innovate tech for their own professional goals, and instead of just documenting the process for their followers, they’re leveraging the audience as a tool to improve the product. 

Earlier this year, VFX creator group Corridor Crew released an open-sourced [green screen tool](https://news.thepublishpress.com/p/why-this-producer-is-leaving-netflix-for-youtube), with over 13K likes on GitHub. The audience was a key source of its success, adjusting the product to take up less computer memory—opening the door for more people to use the tool. Now PewDiePie is employing the same tactic.  

**How it works:** Odysseus has chat, email assistance, and deep research features that run locally on the user’s device, without sharing data to a central company. Odysseus also allows the user to create a “[groupchat](https://youtu.be/lNyICywuyYA?si=kC0PRs_Y8TVFPyIk&t=208)” with different LLMs, comparing answers from other AI models with its own. So far, Odysseus has over 60K likes on GitHub and over 207 contributors to the project.

“I’m releasing it because I want you to help me keep building it,” Kjellberg said in the [announcement video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAzT5lcezPs).

**And it’s working:** At launch, Kjellberg shared that the program couldn’t run on Mac or Windows yet—by the next day, contributors had fixed the issue, expanding availability to most operating systems.

**Looking ahead:** Although PewDiePie and Corridor Crew intend to keep their products free, this method could be used by creators looking to playtest and improve their own paid projects while in beta.

# Inside YouTube’s New Slate of Emmy-Running Creators

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a9f03a5a-b884-4f17-973e-d3a9d5cc42ad/0608_Article_Photo_2.png?t=1780933114)
Caption: Kareem Rahma, Cleo Abram, Julian Shapiro-Barnum, and Brittany Broski pose for YouTube's FYC event at the Television Academy in LA / Photography by Hannah Doyle, [YouTube](https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-emmy-contenders/)

_Hannah here, fresh off a YouTube-filled weekend. _On Friday, I attended YouTube's For Your Consideration (FYC) event at the Television Academy in LA, where Emmy voters gathered to hear pitches from creators Cleo Abram, Brittany Broski, Kareem Rahma, and Julian Shapiro-Barnum for Primetime Emmy consideration.

**Why it matters:** YouTube has run [FYC campaigns](https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/why-youtube-creators-are-emmy-worthy/) for a couple years now, but this cycle feels different—not just because there are more creators, but because of the openness from voters.

During screenings of Rahma’s [Subway Takes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vdICwrN0mkw) and Broski’s [Royal Court](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSkxQslmZ8Q), many in the audience were hollering and laughing. It didn't feel like a room of skeptics. It felt like voters were already sold on the prospect of a creator winning.

**What I heard from voters:**

* Format wasn’t that important to them. They were more interested in the shows’ production quality and the likeability of the creators.

* "I found out about most of these shows through TikTok, but I liked seeing the longer version," one TV producer, who preferred to be anonymous, told me. "These shows have strong production and are worth considering [for an Emmy]."

**After the presentation, creators were sharing why now was their moment for traditional recognition.** "What's changed is the quality has increased so much. It's hard to look at YouTube and say it's not meeting the quality you see on TV,” Cleo Abram said on stage.

_Royal Court _was a prime example. Broski launched the show three years ago with a producer and tables from Party City. Now she has a full crew with writers and set designers—and the show is a staple in the [celebrity](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l9AKB-uT34w&pp=ygULcm95YWwgY291cnQ%3D) [press](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oVVkmPxGtz8) tour. "I don't think there's ever been a successful late night show with a woman at the helm," Broski said. "I'm a product of fan culture. I'm a woman. I didn't see myself up there, so I made it."

**Big picture:** The night confirmed the themes we witnessed at [Press Publish LA](https://www.instagram.com/p/DY5mePixd_u/?hl=en)—audiences _and_ voters are ready to be entertained, no matter the medium. Two weeks ago, Newpress won a [News and Documentary Emmy](https://news.thepublishpress.com/p/these-creators-just-won-an-emmy). A creator's first Primetime Emmy might not be far off. 

“It’s not a new wave,” Abram said. “We’re part of a creative legacy and future, and we’re excited to be a part of an even bigger creative community.”

Happy Monday!

You might have noticed that this email is a day late. I'm writing this from a flight to Boise that I got on as a standby passenger. I was supposed to get to Boise yesterday afternoon, ahead of day 1 of Jay Clouse's Offline Event (a pre-Craft + Commerce event with his Lab community).

But the universe had other plans. I flew into the Dallas airport yesterday around 9:45am, and had a long 3 hour connection. I was prepared for it, though.

Then a quick storm rolled through, and that flight got delayed another 2 hours. No big deal, I can manage.

Then the cancellation email came - due to the storm, it was cancelled. There are only 2 flights out to Boise each day, but thankfully I got rebooked on the 8pm one.

...until that got cancelled too.

I went to the customer service line, and there were at least 75 people ahead of me.

Luckily, I found out that another Lab member, Josh, was also in Dallas going through the same situation. And he was an American Airlines member with access to the lounge, where they had more agents helping people rebook flights, with much shorter lines.

I asked Josh if he could bring a guest in, and thankfully that worked out. A big shoutout to Josh for being so kind!

Long story short, I got rebooked through to Seattle to head to Boise the next morning - and then watched those flights get delayed and delayed, and then cancelled at 8:30pm.

I had been at the airport from 9:30am, a solid 11 hours. I was beat - mentally and physically.

I got a hotel, spent the night in Dallas, and headed back to the airport at 7am to try and get on a standby flight to Boise.

It was a fun day to say the least, but I learned a few things (aside from not booking flights that connect through Dallas again) that are directly related to building a creator business and newsletter:

1. Ask for specific help. I'm notoriously bad at this one, but if I hadn't asked Josh to see if he could get me into the lounge, I would have been waiting around a lot longer.

While there, if I hadn't come to the gate agent with a potential solution to the problem first (connecting through Seattle), they might have said "we don't have any more flights to Boise left" and I'd be out of luck. But since I gave her specific alternatives, it was much easier for her to find a solution.

People are much more likely to help when you ask for something specific.

2. You get what you give. This one came after watching some guy start screaming at a gate agent once the Seattle flight got cancelled. Expletives, blaming - it was pretty bad. After that encounter she said "For all of you waiting in line - if you come up here yelling, I'm going to yell right back."

This ended up being the same very kind woman one who helped rebook me on the last seat out to Boise today. I have so much respect for those folks, who are ultimately problem solvers for people going through some of the worst parts of their day. I'm not sure I'd be able to do that job.

After all, they are human and just want to be treated with respect and kindness. If you give that out first, it's much more likely to be reciprocated.

3. We're all just doing our best. From gate agents, to flight attendants, to the new parents of a crying 2 month old I had the pleasure of sitting next to on this flight - we're all just doing the best we can given the situation. Give people grace.

If someone's not responding to you right away, forgets to do something, or makes a mistake - try and put yourself in their shoes.

You'll be grateful you showed some grace when it's your turn to mess up.
